labels.text: Memory is off: nothing is carried from one conversation to the next on any surface.
Memory is off for your account. Turn it on with `agi memory on`.

S39.02.note: A second, local switch exists in the chat command /memories (row Auto-memory, saved with s); its footer does not mention s, and the account switch is the one that covers all surfaces.
steps: Type agi memory status in a terminal and note the line it prints.
Type agi memory off.
Type agi memory status again.
Compare the last line with Expected: it should say Memory is off, and nothing is carried from one conversation to the next.
S39.02.where: agi memory off, then agi memory on (check with agi memory status)

labels.text: Your AGI account holds no memories in {workspace}.

S39.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one memory (if none, the screen says so)
S39.04.note: There is no full-screen list; the list is printed as plain text in the terminal.
steps: Type agi memory list in a terminal.
Read the header line that gives the number of memories and the workspace name.
Compare the list with Expected: every saved memory should appear, with its text under its topic.

S39.06.note: Topics are sorted alphabetically and come from the category label typed with --category; the code does not pick from a fixed list such as preferences, work or background.
steps: Add two memories with different categories: type agi memory add --category Work <text>, then agi memory add --category Preferences <text>.
Type agi memory list.
Compare with Expected: each topic should appear as its own heading, with its memories under it.
Memories with no category appear under the heading General.

labels.text: Remembered in your account, on every client.

S39.10.note: The in-chat command /memory add writes a local file, not the account memory; this item uses the account command.
steps: Type agi memory add I prefer short answers with bullet points.
Read the line printed back.
Type agi memory list and find the new line.
Compare with Expected: the new fact should be saved and listed.

S39.11.needs: a chat with the assistant and the ability to answer an approval prompt
S39.11.note: This tool saves to the local memory files (global, project or local tiers), so the saved fact does not appear in agi memory list.
steps: Start a chat and type: Remember that I prefer short answers.
When the approval prompt appears, read its text.
Approve it.
Compare with Expected: a confirmation should appear that the item was remembered.
S39.11.where: In a chat with the assistant, type Remember that I prefer short answers, then answer the prompt Remember this in {tier} memory?

S39.12.needs: a chat with the assistant, with Auto-memory set to ON
S39.12.note: The count shown is for local fact files only, and the save is not confirmed on screen; the code gives no other visible sign.
steps: Start the CLI chat and type /memories.
Check that the row Auto-memory shows ON, and note the number in Max facts.
Press Esc, have a normal conversation that states a lasting fact about you, then type /memories again.
Compare with Expected: the stored count should go up, showing that a new fact was saved automatically.

labels.text: Updated in your account, on every client.

S39.13.needs: a saved memory in the account
S39.13.note: Edit is a command, not a menu; there is no edit screen in the chat.
steps: Type agi memory list and copy the id of a memory.
Type agi memory edit <id> <new text>.
Read the line printed back.
Type agi memory list again and compare with Expected: the memory should show the new text under the same id.

labels.text: Forgotten in your account, on every client.

S39.14.needs: a saved memory in the account
S39.14.note: The command is named forget, not delete.
steps: Type agi memory list and copy the id of a memory.
Type agi memory forget <id>.
Read the line printed back.
Type agi memory list and compare with Expected: the memory should no longer be listed.

labels.text: Pinned: this memory is used first.

S39.16.needs: a saved memory in the account
S39.16.note: Pinning is done by command only; there is no pin button in a menu.
steps: Type agi memory pin <id>.
Read the line printed back.
Type agi memory list and look for the star marker at the start of that memory's line.
Compare with Expected: the memory should show as pinned, and the header should say pinned memories are used first.
S39.16.where: agi memory pin <id|text> and agi memory unpin <id|text>

S39.17.needs: a signed-in AGI account; a memory learned from a named chat is needed for the learned-in line
S39.17.note: The origin label is free text from the server or the import source (default Other); the phrase typed by the user is not in the code.
steps: Type agi memory list.
Read the bracket text after each memory id: it shows the origin (default web), the scope and the updated date.
For a memory learned in a chat, read the line learned in '<chat title>' under it.
Compare with Expected: the origin should show where it came from. The code shows only the origin label and the chat title, not the words typed by the user.

S39.18.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one memory
S39.18.note: The date shown is only the first ten characters of the server timestamp.
steps: Type agi memory list.
Read the bracket text after each memory id: it ends with updated and a date (YYYY-MM-DD).
Edit one memory with agi memory edit, then run agi memory list again.
Compare with Expected: the updated date for that memory should be today.

labels.text: Nothing new to import: every memory in that file is already in your account.

S39.21.needs: a text or markdown file with memories to import
S39.21.note: The import runs at once and there is no preview step in the code, although Expected asks for a preview.
steps: Create a plain text or markdown file with a few facts, one per line, in a folder outside the project.
Type agi memory import <file> --source Other.
Read the line printed back.
Type agi memory list and compare with Expected: the new memories should be listed, and later chats should use them.

S39.22.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one memory
S39.22.note: Without --out, the JSON is printed in the terminal. The output is JSON, which may not be the readable file Expected describes.
steps: Type agi memory export --out ~/Desktop/memories-export.json (the file must not exist yet).
Read the line printed back.
Open the file in a text editor.
Compare with Expected: the file should contain every saved memory. It is JSON, not a formatted document.

S39.23.note: Owner decision is open on this item. The count covers local fact files only, and no screen lists memories outside the limit.
steps: Start the CLI chat and type /memories.
Read the Max facts row: it shows how many are stored and the limit, for example [N of 500 stored].
Press Esc.
Compare with Expected: the screen shows the count and limit, but does not list which memories fall outside the limit.

S39.24.needs: a project in the account and a folder linked to it
S39.24.note: A local project tier also exists in the chat command /memory add project <text>; the account list marks other projects as another project.
steps: In a project folder, type agi projects link <project name>.
Type agi memory add --project Our release uses staging first.
Read the line printed back.
Type agi memory list and look for the label this project on that memory.
Compare with Expected: the memory should show as project-only and only that project's chats should use it.
S39.24.where: agi projects link <project>, then agi memory add --project <text>, then agi memory list

labels.text: Your AGI account holds no memories in {workspace}.

S39.26.needs: a second workspace on the same account (the command to switch workspace was not found in the code)
S39.26.note: The code shows the active workspace name only; the switching command was not located in the app's folder.
steps: Type agi memory list and read the header: it names the workspace the memories belong to.
If the account has a second workspace, switch to it and type agi memory list again.
Compare with Expected: each workspace should show only its own memories, with its name in the header.

labels.text: Nothing is on your never-remember list.

S39.29.note: Automatic refusal of credentials is decided by the account server; the app only prints the refusal it returns, and no credential-specific text was found in the app's folder.
steps: Type agi memory never --add salary.
Read the line printed back: it lists the never-remember terms.
Type agi memory add My salary is 90000, then read the refusal line.
Compare with Expected: the sensitive fact should be refused with a Not remembered line.
S39.29.where: agi memory never --add <term>, then agi memory never

labels.text: Remembered in your account, on every client.

S39.31.needs: a signed-in AGI account and access to two models
S39.31.note: Model-independence is enforced in the agent code path, which was not traced to a visible screen.
steps: Type agi memory add I prefer short answers.
Start a chat, switch with /model to one model, and ask what the assistant knows about your answer style.
Switch with /model to a different model, ask the same question.
Compare with Expected: both models should use the same saved memory.
S39.31.where: Effect seen in chat: a memory saved with agi memory add is used after switching model with /model

labels.text: Remembered in your account, on every client.

S39.32.needs: a second client signed in to the same account
S39.32.note: Sync is done by the account server; the CLI prints only the on-every-client line and does not show the other client.
steps: On this machine, type agi memory add I work on the billing team.
On a second client signed in to the same account, look for the memory or ask the assistant about it.
Compare with Expected: the memory should appear and be used there too.
S39.32.where: Effect seen on another client signed in to the same account (for example AGI Mobile or the web app), or via agi memory list on a second machine
